root_cause.text: AppArmor’s `verify_dfa()` in `security/apparmor/match.c` failed to bounds-check `DEFAULT_TABLE` entries for DFA states using differential encoding, allowing a malformed DFA to use an out-of-range default-state index and trigger out-of-bounds access during verification.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `!(BASE_TABLE(dfa)[i] & MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE)` guard so `DEFAULT_TABLE(dfa)[i]` is validated unconditionally, and the CVE text states that when traversing the differential encoding chain `k = DEFAULT_TABLE[j]` was used as an array index “without validation,” causing out-of-bounds reads and writes if `DEFAULT_TABLE[j] >= state_count`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: AppArmor’s `verify_dfa()` in `security/apparmor/match.c` failed to bounds-check `DEFAULT_TABLE` entries for DFA states using differential encoding, allowing a malformed DFA to use an out-of-range default-state index and trigger out-of-bounds access during verification.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes the `!(BASE_TABLE(dfa)[i] & MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE)` guard so `DEFAULT_TABLE(dfa)[i]` is validated unconditionally, and the CVE text states that when traversing the differential encoding chain `k = DEFAULT_TABLE[j]` was used as an array index “without validation,” causing out-of-bounds reads and writes if `DEFAULT_TABLE[j] >= state_count`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten AppArmor DFA verification by always rejecting out-of-bounds default state entries and logging an error.
intent_record.what: In verify_dfa(), the conditional that previously only checked DEFAULT_TABLE(dfa)[i] against state_count when MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE was not set was replaced with an unconditional bounds check. If DEFAULT_TABLE(dfa)[i] is out of range, the code now emits pr_err("AppArmor DFA default state out of bounds") before jumping to out.
intent_record.how: This changes DFA validation so an invalid default-state index is rejected in all cases instead of only for non-diff-encoded states. At runtime, malformed or corrupt AppArmor DFA tables with out-of-bounds default transitions will now be detected and reported consistently, preventing later use of invalid state references.

grouping_result.intent: Tighten AppArmor DFA verification by always rejecting out-of-bounds default state entries and logging an error.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it tightens AppArmor DFA verification to reject out-of-bounds DEFAULT_TABLE/default-state entries, which is the missing bounds check that allowed malformed DFAs to trigger out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: This condition shows that only non-differentially encoded states were checked against DEFAULT_TABLE bounds, leaving differential-encoded DEFAULT_TABLE entries unchecked and allowing an out-of-range default-state index.

This bounds check was limited to the non-differential encoding case, which is the core logic flaw: malformed DFA states using differential encoding could bypass validation and later trigger out-of-bounds access.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional restricts the DEFAULT_TABLE bounds check to only non-differentially encoded states. As a result, malformed DFA entries using differential encoding could bypass verification and later cause out-of-bounds access.
This bounds check is part of the flawed conditional and therefore fails to validate DEFAULT_TABLE entries for differential-encoded states, enabling an out-of-range default-state index.
